summary: Full E2E test of Divr marketing MVP (Next.js 15 + FastAPI + MongoDB). 8/8 backend pytest cases pass against the public preview URL: health, POST /api/waitlist + admin GET, POST /api/operators + admin GET, POST /api/guides + admin GET, plus 3 validation cases (Literal enum + EmailStr 422). Frontend UI tested at 390x844 mobile viewport: home, /waitlist, /for-operators, /for-guides — all required headlines, helper texts, benefit blocks, button labels, and success messages render exactly as specified. All three forms successfully POST to the backend (201) via same-origin fetch and are replaced by the correct success message. Footer renders all required columns/links/copyright/trust line on every page; legal disclaimer is fully visible (not cut off) at 390px. No horizontal scroll on mobile, no console/page errors. MVP is functioning end-to-end.

minor.issue: `logger` is defined at the bottom of the file (line 165) but referenced inside route handlers (lines 63, 93, 126). It works because handlers run after import, but it is fragile — move logging.basicConfig + logger definition above the route handlers.
Unused import: `Optional` from typing is imported but never used.
`@app.on_event("shutdown")` is deprecated in FastAPI ≥ 0.93; prefer the `lifespan` context manager. Non-blocking.

issues: Footer link touch target height is ~22.5px (text-only links). For mobile this is below the recommended 44px minimum tap target. Acceptable for a marketing footer, but worth noting.

All three forms use `noValidate` on <form>, so the browser's native validation is suppressed. Required fields rely solely on backend 422 — frontend currently shows a generic 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' for any non-2xx (no field-level error surfacing). Not a blocker for MVP.

action_items: (Optional) Move logging.basicConfig and `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` to the top of /app/backend/server.py (above the route handlers) for clarity and robustness.
(Optional) Surface field-level validation errors in the three forms instead of a generic 'Something went wrong' message.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is well within the 700-line limit (~170 lines), uses async Motor correctly, excludes _id ({"_id": 0} projection) on all admin GETs, uses Pydantic for input validation including EmailStr and Literal enums for dropdowns, returns proper 201/422 status codes, and reads MONGO_URL/DB_NAME from env.
Frontend uses Next.js 15 App Router + Tailwind correctly. All forms are 'use client', use proper form state, and replace the form on success via a single SuccessMessage component (DRY).
Same-origin /api fetch via lib/api.ts works through the ingress — no CORS issues observed.
All interactive elements (CTAs, form inputs, submits, footer links) have data-testid attributes.
seed_data_creation: No persistent seed data. Each pytest run inserts uniquely-marked TEST_ documents (TEST_wl_<ts>@example.com etc.) into MongoDB collections waitlist_submissions, operator_applications, guide_applications. Browser test additionally inserts ui_wl_/ui_op_/ui_g_ entries. These can be safely cleaned up with: db.waitlist_submissions.deleteMany({email: /^TEST_|^ui_/}), same for the other two collections.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public origin: https://a6522686-f800-45e0-acd7-ed01d9df0901.preview.emergentagent.com — ingress routes /api/* → FastAPI on :8001, everything else → Next.js dev server on :3000. Mongo collections: waitlist_submissions, operator_applications, guide_applications. All POST endpoints return 201 with the persisted entity (id, source, created_at ISO). Admin GETs at /api/admin/{waitlist,operators,guides} return arrays sorted by created_at desc. Forms use noValidate so validation is server-side only (422). Tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_divr_marketing.py and use BASE_URL hardcoded to the public preview origin via conftest.py.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no issues. Note: during the very first browser test attempt, the waitlist form click did not fire a fetch; the cause was that the page was clicked before client-side React hydration finished (no `wait_for_load_state('networkidle')` before the click). After adding the wait, all three form submissions worked on first try and the backend received 201s. This is a test-script issue only and does not affect real users.
